engine: ORION (Borda over RICE, ICE, WSJF, leverage, Eisenhower; judgments by Jev)

rows.label: Fit 4K cameras to the corner masts, aimed along the fence
rows.evidence: Cameras see 63% of the fence line and 69% of the yard (now 2% and 0%). Hard case (drone camera and fence sensor out, intrusion at a random time across equipment charge cycles): intruder met in time 119/120 (95% interval 95%-100%) (now 97/120 (95% interval 73%-87%)), detected after 467 s (now 502 s). The paired runs cannot tell this apart from: Camera masts at the middle of both long sides. Cost: USD 2,000 to USD 8,000 once, nothing a year (assumed: four 4K bullet cameras at $500-2,000 each installed, swapped onto the existing masts and re-aimed along the fence).

rows.label: Re-aim the four corner cameras to look along the fence
rows.evidence: Cameras see 32% of the fence line and 20% of the yard (now 2% and 0%). Hard case (drone camera and fence sensor out, intrusion at a random time across equipment charge cycles): intruder met in time 97/120 (95% interval 73%-87%) (now 97/120 (95% interval 73%-87%)), detected after 502 s (now 502 s). The paired runs cannot tell this apart from: As it is now. Cost: USD 0 to USD 2,000 once, nothing a year (no new equipment; a technician's visit to re-aim four cameras (assumed up to $2,000)).

rows.label: Add a second drone on the patrol circuit
rows.evidence: Hard case (drone camera and fence sensor out, intrusion at a random time across equipment charge cycles): intruder met in time 111/120 (95% interval 86%-97%) (now 97/120 (95% interval 73%-87%)), detected after 298 s (now 502 s). The paired runs cannot tell this apart from: A second guard on foot patrol. A drone is available 73% of the time (now 47%). Cost: USD 15,000 to USD 50,000 once, nothing a year (one surveillance drone at $15,000-50,000 to buy; no subscription price was found).

rows.label: Check fence alarms by drone or robot dog before sending guards
rows.evidence: Over 30 days and 94 nuisance alarms: guards sent 0 times and 0.22 guard hours (114 times and 6.52 hours when everyone responds). Intrusion during a nuisance alarm met in time 38/40 (38/40 when everyone responds). 1 alarms found no machine free. Cost: none; saves about 6 guard hours a month.

rows.label: Add camera masts at the middle of both long sides
rows.evidence: Cameras see 3% of the fence line and 0% of the yard (now 2% and 0%). Hard case (drone camera and fence sensor out, intrusion at a random time across equipment charge cycles): intruder met in time 114/120 (95% interval 89%-98%) (now 97/120 (95% interval 73%-87%)), detected after 465 s (now 502 s). The paired runs cannot tell this apart from: 4K cameras on the four corner masts, aimed along the fence. Cost: USD 12,000 to USD 90,000 once, nothing a year (two installed thermal cameras at $3,000-15,000 each, times 2-3 for poles, cabling, recording and integration).

rows.label: Add a second guard on foot patrol
rows.evidence: Hard case (drone camera and fence sensor out, intrusion at a random time across equipment charge cycles): intruder met in time 113/120 (95% interval 88%-98%) (now 97/120 (95% interval 73%-87%)), detected after 431 s (now 502 s). The paired runs cannot tell this apart from: A second drone on the same circuit. Cost: nothing once, USD 245,280 to USD 367,920 a year (one more post staffed all year at $28-42 an hour fully loaded).

rows.label: Confirm every pickup by phone at the gate before admitting
rows.evidence: Fictitious pickup stopped in 38/40 shifts (12/40 with a paper check); mean wait 9 min (3 min); longest wait 35 min (16 min). The catch rates (0.95 against 0.35) are assumed, not measured. Cost: no equipment; the gate guard's time and the drivers' waiting.

note: Advisory. ORION ranks on the measured evidence above; the costs are rough public price ranges, and the evidence rests on the simulation's stated assumptions.
context:
A synthetic warehouse compound (140 x 100 m, fenced, one gate) on real terrain, simulated: two guards, a robot dog, a patrol vehicle, one drone, four corner camera masts. Guards and machines observe, detect, report and go to meet a person; no force. The site is notional. Goal: decide which improvement to make first. Evidence below is measured in the simulation over 40 seeded runs each; equipment figures and barrier delays are assumptions. Costs are public price ranges, rough and mostly from vendors.
Findings: with all sensors working an intruder is met before finishing in 39/40 runs; with the drone camera out in 38/40. The four corner cameras face outward and see only 2% of the fence line. Weakest direction with the drone out: 45 degrees, met in time 8/40. The single drone is on its charger about half the time.
